transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Nguyen (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Empower Head of Security), Markus Reilly (Infrastructure), Anita Bose (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick SOC 2 / ISO27001 posture review focused on: scope mapping, Trust Center access, KMS/HSM integration options for key management, audit log retention/export for auditors, and a plan for evidence collection. Agreement on follow-ups: Redwood to share specific artifacts and invite audit role to Trust Center; Empower to send infra/residency constraints.

Topics covered:
- Current certification status and desired coverage (SOC 2 Type II + ISO27001 desired)
- Data residency per market and which environments are in scope
- KMS integration: bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed keys and HSM option
- RBAC/SSO onboarding and audit logs (retention, export, and log redaction)
- Evidence collection and timeline for audit readiness

Action items (captured during call): see metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm avery from redwood, i'm the account lead for empower — quick round the table?
[00:12] Lena (Empower): hi lena here, head of security, uh we've got markus and anita with me. thanks.
[00:18] Priya (Redwood SE): priya — i'll run technical bits, especially KMS and logs side.
[00:22] Markus (Empower): markus — infra lead, we'll be doing the network and residency mapping.
[00:26] Anita (Empower): anita — compliance, i'll be coordinating evidence.
[00:30] Avery: awesome. quick agenda: where you are today on soc two and iso, what you need from redwood to satisfy auditors, and then a small deep dive — priya will cover kms options.
[00:42] Lena: sure, right now we have SOC 2 Type II in our vendor stack for some services, but we need coverage of inference endpoints and data flows. iso27001 is in flight at corporate but we need mapping for this product.
[00:55] Priya: got it. to confirm—are you planning to run redwood in hosted mode or private (vpc/on-prem)?
[01:02] Lena: preference is private VPC for regulated markets, hosted for lower risk. we'll need residency controls for eu and apac customers.
[01:12] Priya: makes sense. we support private deployment with a control-plane in your vpc or a redwood-managed trust center access — there are two KMS patterns: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with your KMS/HSM or use Redwood-managed keys.
[01:27] Markus: can you expand on BYOK — we use AWS KMS with multi-account keys and have HSM-backed keys for some jurisdictions.
[01:35] Priya: yep — BYOK lets you maintain key policies and rotation via your KMS, redwood will call out to your key using an encrypted key-encryption-key (KEK) flow. there is also an HSM-backed option where the keys never leave your HSM. quick caveat: BYOK requires some network egress rules if you use redwood hosted control plane; private deployment reduces that need.
[01:55] Anita: auditors ask for key custody proofs — do you provide attestation or details for HSM usage?
[02:02] Priya: we can provide architecture diagrams, KMS call traces, and a pattern for evidence — also our SOC 2 report includes sections describing key management controls. we'll share a redacted SOC 2 Type II excerpt after this call.
[02:16] Avery: i'll add that to the next steps.
[02:19] [small crosstalk]
[02:25] Lena: on logs — we need audit logs for all inference requests retained for 12 months and exportable to our SIEM — is that possible?
[02:33] Priya: yes we capture audit trails at request and system levels. by default hosted retains 90 days, dedicated and private options allow custom retention. export to S3 or push to your SIEM (via syslog / HTTPS ingestion). there are also redaction hooks so PII isn't retained.
[02:52] Markus: syslog is preferred. our auditors want proof-of-delivery and hash verification of logs, how do you support immutability?
[03:01] Priya: we can output logs to an S3 bucket in your account (private deployment), and you can enable object lock/immutability there. for hosted, we offer signed digests and a retention export workflow. (note: transcript sometimes shows 'signed digests' as 'signed digest' in the recordings)
[03:18] Anita: ok. evidence chain is critical. we'll need to know who in redwood has access to the trust center and audit trails.
[03:25] Avery: we have role-based access — we'll map roles to the least privilege model. priya will share a role mapping doc. i'll invite your audit mailbox to read-only roles in trust center.
[03:37] Lena: good. important: separation of duties — provisioning vs ops.
[03:41] Priya: yep, we support SSO (SAML) and SCIM for user provisioning, and role maps can be enforced with RBAC.
[03:49] Markus: slightly worried about network egress, does redwood need persistent outbound to third-party endpoints for KMS when using BYOK?
[03:57] Priya: in hosted mode yes, there is occasional egress to call your KMS endpoint. with private control plane in your VPC or fully on-prem, those calls stay inside your network.
[04:08] Markus: got it. for residency — can we pin inference to eu-west-1 and restrict token storage to eu?
[04:15] Priya: yes you can pin model execution regionally and configure data residency. logs and telemetry can be routed to your region and your S3 buckets. we'll document the config we used for a similar customer.
[04:26] Anita: regarding artifact delivery — auditors want the latest SOC report and a control mapping matrix. do you maintain a controls <-> artifact map?
[04:34] Avery: yes we have a controls matrix mapping Redwood controls to SOC 2 / ISO clauses and the evidence artifacts. priya will send the latest.
[04:42] [00:04:45 small phone noise]
[04:46] Priya: quick live screen share? i can show the trust center briefly — (screen share starts).
[04:52] [screen noise / micro-silence]
[05:00] Priya: on the trust center home — you'll see compliance reports, roles, and audit logs section. we can grant read-only access to your auditors, and you can download signed report bundles. link (redacted): https://trust.redwood.example/empower-audit
[05:19] Lena: perfect. what level of PII redaction exists? sometimes inference prompts include customer data.
[05:27] Priya: we have prompt redaction hooks and schema-level redaction. we recommend using prefix hashing for user IDs and applying client-side transforms for sensitive fields. we'll attach our prompt redaction guide.
[05:42] Markus: relates to KV cache — does cache ever persist user content outside of the region?
[05:48] Priya: by default kv cache is in-region; for hosted some cache layers may be shared but they are encrypted; private deployments keep cache fully in your vpc. the audio transcriber sometimes wrote "K V" as "kay vee" in previous notes.
[06:02] Anita: how about incident response? auditor wants timeline of one incident last year — can you provide redwood's incident postmortems?
[06:09] Avery: we share redacted postmortems and SLA history for customers under NDA — we'll coordinate with legal.
[06:16] Lena: the compliance timeline — we plan external audit in Q1 2027. we need Redwood evidence by end of Q4 2026 to prepare. feasible?
[06:24] Priya: yes, if we start evidence handoff now we can meet that timeline. good to lock the role invites and KMS plan this week.
[06:32] [07:00] Markers of slight interruption — speaker overlap
[07:05] Priya: technical deep-dive notes — KMS flows: 1) BYOK with AWS KMS cross-account grants, 2) HSM with external appliance and KMS proxies, 3) Redwood managed keys with customer tenancy — each has tradeoffs on auditability and lead time.
[07:20] Markus: for option 2 (HSM) would that require a hardware appliance at our data center?
[07:25] Priya: optionally yes. or you can use cloud HSM services; integration patterns differ slightly. we'll provide a comparison table.
[07:33] Anita: auditors will ask who can rotate keys — we need a rotation policy and proof-of-execution.
[07:39] Priya: rotation can be triggered by your KMS and rotation events are logged. we'll include sample rotation logs as part of the evidence bundle.
[07:48] Avery: question for you — any markets with absolute prohibition on data leaving national boundaries (e.g., some APAC countries)?
[07:56] Lena: singapore and occasionally indonesia customers ask for data to stay in-country, but mainly our EU and AUS obligations matter right now.
[08:05] Priya: we can pin data to region and ensure logs do not leave region; need a small configuration change and a dedicated deployment for high-assurance markets.
[08:14] Markus: what about network peering costs and management?
[08:18] Priya: private deployment uses VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink — there are egress cost tradeoffs; we'll include estimated costs in the follow-up.
[08:27] [08:30] Anita: about the controls matrix — can you map to our internal control IDs?
[08:33] Avery: yes we'll accept your mapping sheet — tom (csm) will coordinate the upload and mapping pointers.
[08:40] Tom (Redwood CSM): i'll be the single point for evidence ingestion and can set up a shared drive.
[08:46] Lena: thanks. also curious — if we do a pilot, can we run some sample requests and capture full audit logs for the auditors to review?
[08:55] Priya: absolutely, pilot mode can enable full verbose logging and we can produce a signed log bundle after the run. note: the transcript may show 'signed log bundle' sometimes as 'sing log' — small ASR noise.
[09:07] Markus: for the pilot, we want to test latency under residency constraints — will your private deployment support GPU autoscaling?
[09:16] Priya: yes dedicated GPU pools with autoscaling are supported; for private we provide a scalable cluster template. we will share config sample.
[09:26] Anita: evidence retention policy — if we export to our S3 with object lock, is it straightforward to snapshot and hand over to auditors?
[09:34] Priya: yes, snapshots are straightforward and we can attach digests for verification. for hosted we provide the signed exports.
[09:40] Lena: competitors: i know BigCloud AI offers BYOK but their audit docs were thin; any notable gaps you see?
[09:48] Avery: one thing customers call out is lack of clear controls mapping in competitor material. we try to present a clear control->artifact matrix.
[09:55] [10:00] Anita: on SSO — we use Okta; provisioning must be SCIM based and groups map to roles. are there any gaps?
[10:06] Priya: Okta + SCIM is fully supported. we'll share the SCIM mapping doc and sample SAML metadata.
[10:13] Markus: small nit — do you provide role-based audit logs that show who initiated a model deployment?
[10:19] Priya: yes, deployment audit logs include user, role, timestamp and the action payload (hashes only). full payload can be redacted.
[10:28] Lena: good. i want to confirm: trust center access — is it multi-tenant? can we assign a read-only auditor role that only sees our artifacts?
[10:36] Priya: yes, read-only auditor role is scoped by account and project. we'll show role scoping live in the trust center.
[10:44] Tom: i'll coordinate the invite list. can we get a sample invite link after the call?
[10:49] Avery: yes, action item — i'll send the invite link and role docs.
[10:53] [11:00] brief pause while screens shared
[11:05] Priya: showing KMS diagram — (note: spoken word had 'kay vee' references for cache). diagram includes key flow, rotation, and audit events pushed to CloudWatch or Splunk.
[11:18] Markus: for rotation, would you allow cross-account rotation keys? we have multi-account landing zones.
[11:25] Priya: yes, you can use cross-account grants or a centralized key account. both patterns supported.
[11:32] Anita: do you have a recommended naming convention and tag policy for key provenance? auditors love consistent tags.
[11:37] Priya: yes we'll provide tag examples and a script to validate tags during evidence collection.
[11:44] Lena: timeline again — we'll want artifacts by EoQ4 2026. is that on the table?
[11:50] Priya: yes if we get the infra diagram and residency list this week we can package artifacts.
[11:55] Avery: ok we'll aim for that.
[12:00] [12:10] crosstalk about scheduling next deep-dive
[12:15] Avery: propose follow-up week of Dec 7th for logs deep-dive — okay?
[12:20] Lena: works for us.
[12:23] Markus: one last question — can we have non-repudiation for logs? the hash-based digests are sufficient?
[12:30] Priya: yes, we can provide signed hashes and chain-of-custody documentation.
[12:36] Anita: thanks everyone. last ask: include a clear list of artifacts for our auditors (SOC 2 excerpt, key rotation logs, trust center roles, signed log exports, controls mapping).
[12:48] Priya: will do — i'll assemble the bundle and drop to the shared drive.
[12:52] Avery: recap and next steps: 1) redwood to share SOC 2 excerpt and ISO control map; 2) priya to send KMS diagrams + terraform samples; 3) avery to add audit mailbox to trust center; 4) empow-er to return residency list and infra diagram. we'll capture deadlines in an email.
[13:12] Lena: perfect, thanks — great call.
[13:16] Avery: thanks all, talk soon.
[13:20] [meeting ends]

References / artifacts mentioned:

- Controls mapping template: /redwood-shared/empower/controls-mapping-template.xlsx

Avery: 'We'll share the SOC 2 Type II excerpt and invite the audit mailbox to Trust Center this week. Priya will assemble KMS artefacts and terraform samples. Empower will give us their residency list and infra diag.'
